picks.file: Map of Zurich by Braun Hogenberg (34065120).jpg
picks.what: Engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 3
picks.who: Georg Braun and Frans Hogenberg, after Jos Murer
picks.why: colored bird’s-eye view; Limmat, Grossmünster and Fraumünster clear; highest-resolution copy, already cut to the plate (from the 1616 edition)

picks.file: Gezicht op Zürich, 1726 La Ville de Zurich, en Profil (titel op object) Les Forces de l'Europe, Asie, Afrique et Amerique Comme aussi les Cartes des Côtes de France et d'Espagne (serietitel op objec, RP-P-OB-83.036-90.jpg
picks.what: View from the lake, engraving in Les Forces de l’Europe, Asie, Afrique et Amerique
picks.why: lake front with the minster towers; trimmed to the plate

picks.file: Zentralbibliothek Zürich - Handwerkskundschaft der Zunft der Buchbinder - 991037222059705501.jpg
picks.what: View from the lake, etching on a guild journeyman’s certificate (Zentralbibliothek Zürich)
picks.why: panorama ‘drawn from nature 1765’; trimmed to the picture above the certificate text

picks.file: BAZ - Blick auf das untere Limmatquai.tiff
picks.what: The Limmatquai and Niederdorf with the Polytechnikum, photograph (Baugeschichtliches Archiv Zürich)
picks.why: general view from a height over the old town and river to the ETH building

picks.file: ETH-BIB-Zürich, Hauptbahnhof, Landesmuseum, Limmat aus 100 m-Inlandflüge-LBS MH01-001793.tif
picks.what: The main station, Landesmuseum and Limmat, aerial photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: high resolution; station hall and Landesmuseum instantly recognizable

picks.what: View down the Limmat from the Quaibrücke, photograph
picks.why: Fraumünster, St. Peter and Grossmünster in one sunny frame; very high resolution

gaps: P0: nothing. P3 has only 1765; nothing from 1770–1849.
notes: P2 (#13, 1726) re-engraves Merian’s 1642 view from the lake, so it shows the city as of about 1640; drop it if a derivative is unwanted (Merian’s own 1642 plate, #4, is the alternative but shares P1 with Braun and Hogenberg). The same 1765 Metzger view without the certificate (#19) shows the Grossmünster towers burning (the 1763 lightning fire), so I used the ordinary version. #27 (photochrom from the Utoquai, 1890s) is a color alternative for P4 but the city is small in the frame. #10, #12 and #20 are paintings of other places held in the Kunsthaus; #11 is Eglisau.
